overview: This House resolution sets the ground rules for debating four bills, which is how the House usually brings major legislation to the floor. It covers the annual Defense Department spending bill for the budget year starting October 2025 (H.R. 4016), a bill setting up regulation of digital assets such as cryptocurrencies by the Securities and Exchange Commission and the Commodity Futures Trading Commission (H.R. 3633), a bill barring the Federal Reserve from offering a central bank digital currency (H.R. 1919), and a Senate-passed bill regulating stablecoins, which are digital tokens tied to the value of a currency like the dollar (S. 1582). For each, it limits debate time and which amendments can be offered, and it sets aside certain procedural objections. It also lets the House take up, on the same day, a rule for a bill canceling some previously approved spending at the President's request. The House adopted it by a vote of 217 to 212 on July 16, 2025.
for: Supporters say it lets the House move efficiently on government funding and on long-awaited rules for digital assets, while still allowing debate and a set of amendments.
against: Critics say it tightly limits amendments and waives normal procedural protections, cutting short debate on major and complex financial and defense legislation.
